transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date: 2027-11-16
- Start: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 46 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan, Priya (Redwood); Liam, Maya, Thomas (QuestorX)

Summary: quick discovery focused on how QuestorX would integrate Redwood behind a gateway/proxy. Customers curious about hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) for compliance, SDK support (LangChain/LlamaIndex), rate limits and observability hooks.

Topics:
- Integration patterns (sidecar/proxy vs direct SDK)
- LangChain / LlamaIndex examples and adapters
- Rate limits, quotas and burst capacity
- Observability hooks / tracing / token-level costs
- Security: SSO, KMS, audit logs

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): ok thanks everyone for joining, i'm jordan from redwood, quick intro from us then we want to understand your current stack and success criteria, maybe we can start with you liam?
[00:12] Liam (CTO): yeah, thanks. we're QuestorX, we run a platform that does guided search over customer docs, so heavy embedding pipeline and some chat flows. latency matters, but so does cost — we do multi-tenant, lots of requests nightly.
[00:28] Priya (SE): got it. are you calling models through an intermediary gateway or direct from your app today?
[00:34] Maya (ML Eng): currently we have an nginx gateway that proxies to a mix of cloud endpoints and a handful of self-hosted GPUs for big jobs. we also use LangChain in some microservices, and a couple teams toy with LlamaIndex.
[00:45] Jordan: that maps to what we see. curious — what's the main pain with the nginx proxy today?
[00:51] Thomas (Platform): operational overhead, routing rules are messy, and batching is non-existent. also hard to instrument token-level billing and cost per route.
[01:05] Priya: ok makes sense — with redwood you have a few options: hosted api (fast to start), dedicated reserved pools (predictable throughput), or a private vpc/on-prem for strict compliance. we can put a lightweight proxy in front as a sidecar or you can call the sdk directly.
[01:25] Liam: sidecar vs sdk — what's the tradeoff?
[01:28] Priya: sidecar (gateway) gives centralized routing, rate limiting, and consistent observability; SDK is simpler for devs and integrates with langchain adapters directly. sidecar helps if you want cross-team routing policies and easier fallback to cheaper model variants.
[01:46] Maya: we specifically want to keep latency P50 under 250ms on short chat requests — is that realistic on hosted?
[01:52] Jordan: depends on model and region, but for many of the smaller open models we see 120–200ms P50 under light load; dedicated can give you tighter bounds and burst capacity. we can show sample numbers in the pricing sheet.
[02:05] [brief crosstalk — someone unmuted]
[02:12] Priya: about langchain/llamaindex — we have example adapters in our repo. they expose a Connector interface so you can swap between calling the redwood sdk directly or hitting a local gateway. note: auto-generated docs sometimes call it LamaIndex, so please forgive the transcription.
[02:34] Maya: will those adapters preserve streaming and function-calling behavior?
[02:38] Priya: yes, streaming is supported; function calling and structured outputs are supported via the same sdk; the sidecar exposes streaming endpoints too but you need to wire the websocket through your gateway. we have examples for node/python.
[02:55] Liam: what about rate limits — we have spikes when users run large batch imports. can we throttle per-tenant?
[03:03] Jordan: yes — per-api-key and per-route quotas are standard. for dedicated pockets you can set guaranteed throughput and burst limits. we also support route-based routing policies that can fallback to cheaper quantized variants when under pressure.
[03:20] Thomas: curious about KV cache — we've seen the term in your docs — how is that exposed through the proxy?
[03:27] Priya: the runtime manages kv-cache for autoregressive flows; the gateway can preserve cached prefixes if you route the same session. occasionally the transcript says kay-vee cache, but its kay vee. you can also set sticky sessions to keep cache warm on dedicated nodes.
[03:44] Maya: observability — we need tracing, token-level cost breakdowns, and audit logs for compliance. can we hook into datadog and our internal tracing?
[03:53] Priya: yes — we emit tracing headers and have integrations for opentelemetry, datadog and prometheus metrics. token-level cost reports are in the console and exported via API. for private deployments you can keep the control plane on-prem and push audit logs to your SIEM.
[04:12] Liam: security checklist — do you have SOC2, SSO, KMS integrations?
[04:18] Jordan: yep — SOC2 and ISO are in our security pack, SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning, and KMS/HSM options for private installs. i'll drop the security doc after the call (link sent).
[04:31] Thomas: when you say private — is that fully on-prem or VPC with customer-managed networking?
[04:36] Priya: both. VPC private deployment keeps the control plane hosted but data plane in your VPC, or fully on-prem for air-gapped. depends on your compliance needs.
[04:50] Maya: for LangChain — do you see customers using the SDK directly inside chains or using the gateway adapter? any gotchas?
[04:56] Priya: both patterns are used. direct SDK -> faster dev iteration; gateway gives centralized policy enforcement. gotchas: streaming with some langchain connectors needs small changes, and some LlamaIndex write-ups reference older APIs. we'll share a short migration note.
[05:15] Liam: can we run a small proof: hosted endpoint first, run a 50 rps synthetic load for 24 hours, share logs and costs, then decide on dedicated?
[05:22] Jordan: absolutely — that's our typical path. we can provision a test key, suggest a load profile, and Priya will give the bench script.
[05:30] Maya: any limits on payload size or embedding batch sizes? we do 10k token contexts sometimes for document search.
[05:36] Priya: for very long contexts we recommend chunking and using embeddings + retrieval. dedicated nodes have higher memory profiles; for hosted we have max request size limits — we'll share the exact numbers.
[05:46] Thomas: what's your SLA for dedicated? 99.9?
[05:50] Jordan: we offer SLA-backed uptime for dedicated contracts, typically 99.9 with escalation and support SLAs in enterprise tier.
[05:58] [00:06:00 marker — mid-call recaps]
[06:00] Jordan: recap — action items are: pricing + options, langchain/llamaindex adapters, bench script, and customer to share prompts and P50 targets. we'll also send security pack. anything else?
[06:14] Liam: can you include an example of fallback policy where requests flip to a smaller quantized model if dedicated nodes are saturated? that's important for our SREs.
[06:22] Priya: yes — i'll include a couple of policy examples and a traffic shaping playbook.
[06:28] Maya: oh and one more — token cost per-embed vs per-token generation breakdown, want to plug into our chargeback model.
[06:34] Jordan: noted. we'll add it to the spreadsheet.
[06:40] [closing minute — scheduling follow up]
[06:42] Jordan: we'll aim to send everything by thursday, can we do a check-in next tuesday to review the bench results?
[06:48] Liam: tuesday works. thanks all.
[06:50] Jordan: great thanks, talk soon.
